title: Insurance RiskOps Sellframe & Battlecard — Sprint Sketch
content:
Overview (speaker note): Quick internal sketch for a short sales deck + one-page battlecard aimed at Risk Operations / Claims teams at insurers and insurtechs. Purpose: give AE/SE a tight narrative for discovery calls and a single-sheet cheat that highlights Redwood Inference fit for regulated inference workloads (policy review, fraud detection, claims triage). Status: early sprint sketch — lots of TODOs, needs data from Solutions Eng (latency numbers on sample model) and Finance (example pricing scenarios).

Slide 1 — Hook / one-liner:
- Title: Make automated risk review fast, predictable, and auditable
- Bullets: Reduce claims triage time while keeping full auditability and controls. Pinpoint use-cases: claims intake triage, automated suspicious-activity flags, regulatory reporting prep.
- Speaker note: Lead with a pain: "Claims backlog -> higher payouts & slower settlements" and then number: "We help you cut average initial triage time by X and reduce human review volume by Y% (example metrics to replace)."

Slide 2 — Problem framing for RiskOps (discovery prompts):
- Fragmented tooling: models running ad-hoc, inconsistent latency, noisy cost spikes
- Regulatory constraints: PHI/PII handling, audit logging, retention policies
- Discovery questions for AE: "How do you currently route suspicious claims? What SLA on triage latency do teams expect? How much of review is manual vs. automated?"
- Speaker tip: use discovery to map to Redwood features: private deployment, audit logs, and rollouts.

Slide 3 — Redwood value props mapped to RiskOps:
- Predictable latency at scale: Dedicated pools + autoscaling policies for steady throughput
- Data residency & controls: Private deployment (VPC) + KMS integration for encrypted keys
- Cost levers that preserve quality: Automatic caching, batching suggestions, quantization profiles for near-linear cost reductions
- Observability: Per-route token cost, end-to-end traces, and regression alerts tied to prompt sets

Slide 4 — Quick technical fit / integration notes:
- Typical flow: claims intake -> preprocessor -> Redwood inference (triage model) -> flags + KV cache for repeated policies -> human review queue if threshold
- Integration touchpoints: webhooks for async responses, SDKs for Java/Python, audit log S3 export, model pinning for controlled rollouts
- Deployment options: Hosted API for pilots, Dedicated for predictable production throughput, Private for regulated PII/PHI workloads
- Speaker note: call out that Dedicated pools are best for predictable throughput and consistent tail latency required by fraud detection.

Slide 5 — Example ROI sketch (placeholder numbers):
- Baseline: 200k claims/month, avg manual triage 5 min/claim, 3 FTE dedicated to triage
- Expected with automation + Redwood: reduce manual triage volume by 40%, average handling time cut to 1.5 min for escalations
- Result: estimated reduction of 2 FTEs + faster settlements -> faster repayments and NPS uplift
- Cost side: show hosted pilot cost vs dedicated commit example. (Finance to fill with accurate per-token and seat pricing)

Slide 6 — Competitive differentiation (talking points instead of callouts):
- Not just "model hosting": emphasis on production economics (observability, batching knobs, cache, fallback routing)
- Unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private: fewer engineering pieces to assemble vs building in-house
- Play safe on claims: customers can run sensitive flows in private deployments + bring-your-own-key
- Objection triggers: if buyer compares to large cloud vendor managed endpoints, focus on inference-centered tooling and SLO controls rather than raw cloud compute list prices.

Slide 7 — Battlecard / one-pager quick reference (front-facing cheat):
- Target persona: Head of RiskOps, Claims Ops Lead, Platform/ML infra lead
- Pain they feel: spikes in review backlog, unpredictable model costs, compliance risk with PII
- Quick ask in discovery: "If you could guarantee X ms tail latency and a 30% reduction in human review, would that change your rollout plans?"
- Top 3 Redwood proof points to call out: private deployments + audit logs, rollout controls (canary/A-B + automatic fallback), cost-saving kit (caching + batch + quantization guidance)
- 60s elevator script: "Redwood gives you a single runtime to run production LLMs that meets your latency, compliance and cost guardrails so you can automate risk review without building a bespoke serving stack."

Slide 8 — Objection handling, quick scripts:
- Objection: "We cannot send PII to hosted APIs." Response: "We offer private deployment and VPC options with customer-managed keys; we can also run an on-prem package for fully air-gapped evaluation."
- Objection: "We already have models running on cloud endpoints." Response: "You can migrate traffic gradually — Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to existing endpoints while we show cost/latency gains on a slice of production traffic."
- Objection: "How do we prove quality hasn’t regressed?" Response: "Ship prompt sets and eval hooks; Redwood Optimize ties regressions to alerts and model rollbacks."

Slide 9 — Enablement checklist for AE/SE pre-call:
- Ask for: expected daily traffic, acceptable tail latency, data residency needs, existing stack (message bus, data lake), current cost per 100k tokens if they track it
- Demo prep: have a canned triage prompt + sample CSV of 20 sample claims (anonymized) for live demo
- Collateral to send after call: one-pager, link to private deployment brief, example ROI template

Appendix — Live demo script + short prompt examples (for SE):
- Prompt (claims triage): "Given the claim text and metadata, assign a triage score from 0-100 and list 3 reasons for escalation."
- Example live flow for demo: upload sample CSV -> call Redwood hosted sandbox model -> show streaming tokens + per-token cost in console -> flip to dedicated preview and compare latency profile

Open items / TODOs:
- Replace placeholder ROI numbers with Finance-approved scenarios and produce two committed pricing options (pilot vs committed dedicated).
- Solutions Eng to run latency profile on sample ensembles for triage model (90th/95th/99th).
- Legal to provide recommended wording for PII handling in customer-facing battlecard.
- Populate a 1-pager PDF export and one-line email templates for follow-up (next sprint).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this short (one deck + one-sheet); AEs appreciate tight scripts.
- Avoid heavy model-architecture talk on first call — focus on outcomes & controls.
- Sync with Field Enablement next Tues for roleplay.

End of sketch — feedback welcome.
